summary: Interim report. On web-01 the site plugin had a hidden, hand-copied file inc/rental-quote.php (not in the ci-01 repo). Posting a magic 'ref' value returned the WordPress DB credentials from wp-config.php, and the file also let a caller test DB passwords. 174.62.132.218 posted straight to this file and nothing else on Nov 1 and Nov 10, and both times got 247-byte responses. That size matches the credential dump, not a normal quote, so I treat the site DB password as stolen. The wp_larkspur account only accepts connections from 10.20.0.x, and I found no SSH or database activity from that IP. Done so far: moved the backdoor to /root/quarantine (it now returns 404); rotated app-db-password and updated the second copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf (the site and the report job work). Hardening on web-01: removed deploy's 'sudo rsync' (a root escalation); took the jpark account (not in the staff directory, had sudo, no logins) out of sudo and locked it; changed the root cron job larkspur-orders so it no longer executes wp-config.php or uses eval (deploy owned that file, so deploy could become root), and wp-config.php is now root:www-data 640; made larkspur-mailing-export write its CSV as the requesting user (it was a root symlink/chown escalation); nginx now refuses PHP under wp-content/uploads. Still investigating ci-01 and db-01.

Updated report. web-01 had two backdoors, and both were used from outside. (1) The must-use plugin wp-content/mu-plugins/agency-support.php (from the former agency Blue Ridge Web Co) passed the request's 'path' to shell_exec without any login, so anyone could run commands as www-data with POST / asup=purge&path=;cmd. 172.56.38.75 sent one POST to / at 14:05:03 today, right after the VM restart, and nothing else. The 159-byte reply is neither the 'env' output (148 bytes) nor the default reply (14 bytes), so it was most likely command output. I found no processes, changed files or planted code from it. (2) inc/rental-quote.php in the site plugin returned the DB credentials from wp-config.php; 174.62.132.218 used it on Nov 1 and Nov 10. Containment and rotation: the original mu-plugin and rental-quote.php are in /root/quarantine on web-01. The mu-plugin is replaced by a safe version (cache purge in PHP, only inside wp-content/cache, no DB details), so Switchback's support tool (96.255.239.206) keeps working. Rotated app-db-password (and updated the copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf) and shuffled the WordPress salts (Maria and Lucia need to log in to wp-admin again). Hardening: Grafana 8.3.1 (CVE-2021-43798 file read, no fixed package in the mirror) now listens on 127.0.0.1:3001 behind nginx on :3000, which blocks traversal; PHP is blocked under uploads; deploy's sudo rsync removed; the larkspur-orders root cron no longer executes wp-config.php; wp-config.php is now root:www-data 640; mailing-export symlink escalation fixed; jpark (not in the staff directory) removed from sudo and locked on web-01 and ci-01, and demoted from WordPress administrator with a random password; deploy's CI key on web-01 limited to from=10.20.0.30, and db-01's backup key on ci-01 to from=10.20.0.20; the internal maint.d folder is no longer writable by www-data or deploy. On ci-01: the repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable (now root:developers 0640), and root's 'git gc' on the developer-writable repo now runs as deploy. Note: in my first test of the replacement, PHP's opcache still served the old file, my injection test really ran, and it removed the empty wp-content/cache folder; I restored it. Releases, dumps to ci-01, payouts, report and orders all still work. I found no signs of intrusion on db-01 or ci-01. Logins there are staff from their usual addresses.

FINAL. An outsider got in to web-01; I found no sign that db-01 or ci-01 were reached.

WHAT HAPPENED
1) wp-content/mu-plugins/agency-support.php (from the former agency Blue Ridge Web Co, loaded on every request) passed the request's 'path' to shell_exec with no login, so anyone could run commands as www-data (POST / asup=purge&path=;cmd). 172.56.38.75 sent a single POST / at 14:05:03 today and got a 159-byte reply. That is neither the 'env' output (148 bytes) nor the default reply (14), so it was most likely command output. The IP tried again at 14:17:20, after my fix, and got an empty reply. I found no planted files, processes or code from it.
2) wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php (hand-copied, never in the ci-01 repo) returned the WordPress DB credentials from wp-config.php when sent a magic 'ref'. 174.62.132.218 posted straight to it and nothing else on Nov 1 and Nov 10, and both replies were the credential-dump size.
The only secrets www-data could read were in wp-config.php: the DB password and the WordPress salts.

CONTAINMENT AND ROTATION
- rental-quote.php moved to /root/quarantine on web-01, and its removal committed in web-01's local plugin git (Maria's 14:04 'git add -A' had committed it).
- agency-support.php replaced with a safe version: cache purge done in PHP only inside wp-content/cache, 'env' no longer shows DB details. The original is in quarantine. Switchback's support tool (96.255.239.206) keeps working.
- Rotated app-db-password and updated the second copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf. Shuffled the WordPress salts, so Maria and Lucia need to log in to wp-admin again.
- No other secret showed signs of being read, so I did not rotate the payment key, deploy password, bucket key, GitHub token or the root secrets.

HARDENING (web-01)
- Grafana 8.3.1 has CVE-2021-43798, an unauthenticated file read, and has no fixed package in the mirror. It now listens on 127.0.0.1:3001 behind nginx on :3000, which blocks traversal; live scans now get 400.
- PHP execution blocked under wp-content/uploads.
- Removed deploy's 'sudo rsync' (a root escalation).
- The larkspur-orders root cron no longer runs wp-config.php through php and eval. wp-config.php is now root:www-data 640.
- larkspur-mailing-export now writes as the requesting user (it was a root symlink/chown escalation).
- jpark (not in the staff directory) removed from sudo and locked on web-01 and ci-01, and demoted from WordPress administrator with a random password.
- The CI key in deploy's authorized_keys is limited to from=10.20.0.30.
- The internal maint.d folder and the plugin's .git are no longer writable by www-data. Planted hooks or config there could have taken over Maria's or deploy's account.

HARDENING (ci-01)
- The repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable; it is now root:developers 0640.
- Root's 'git gc' on the developer-writable repo now runs as deploy.
- db-01's backup key is limited to from=10.20.0.20.

MY MISTAKE
The first test of the replaced mu-plugin ran against PHP's cached copy of the old file. My test command really ran and removed wp-content/cache, which held only an empty index.html. I restored it.

LEFT OPEN FOR MARIA
- deploy accepts password logins from the internet. 35.196.129.99 uses it about every 5 hours with no failed attempts; this matches the 'old monitoring box' that rotate-secret lists as holding the deploy password.
- Staff password logins are on server-wide.
- offsite-backup and offsite were already failing before my shift (no internet route).

CHECKED AFTER ALL CHANGES
Release every 3 minutes OK, dumps to ci-01 OK (14:20), payout check OK, settle batch at 14:22 sent 10 payouts, site, wp-admin login and Grafana work.
